name: unixnames
description: A SOCKET'S NAME IS AS LONG AS AF_UNIX'S.  unixprobe -n binds two stream sockets to 40-character paths and asks for names with a 110-byte buffer: getsockname, getpeername and accept must each return the whole 42-byte name and write 42 back, as 2.11BSD's uipc_syscalls.c copies min(*len, m_len).  A 16-byte buffer gets 16 bytes and 16, with the byte after it untouched (Review Focus 4: never an overrun).  A datagram sender's name is one struct sockaddr, as 2.11BSD's sbappendaddr copies it, so recvfrom gets 16 bytes from a 110-byte buffer and 8 from an 8-byte one.  CONTROL, measured: the kernel ignoring the caller's length writes the whole name into the 16-byte buffer and fails `sockname16'.
